title: Ask AI for Failure Cases Before You Ship
subtitle: Use the model as an adversarial idea generator, then turn useful candidates into real checks
description: Give AI a feature, process, calculation, message, or workflow and ask for edge cases and failure modes. Treat the output as a candidate list, deduplicate it, verify relevance, and convert the useful cases into executable tests or checklist items.

lifeOsSource.hack: Ask AI to generate edge cases and failure modes, then promote only verified candidates into tests or checks.
lifeOsSource.whatYouDo: Describe the intended behavior, constraints, known happy path, and expensive failures. Ask for boundary cases, invalid inputs, state transitions, concurrency or timing issues where relevant, and user misunderstandings. Remove duplicates, verify each candidate against the real system, and write tests for the cases worth keeping.
lifeOsSource.checkIn: Did AI expose a failure I had not covered, and did I turn that idea into a check rather than merely admire the list?

faq.question: Are generated test cases evidence that a bug exists?
faq.answer: No. They are hypotheses about where the system could fail. Reproduce or validate the condition before treating it as a defect.

faq.question: What context helps most?
faq.answer: State the contract, boundaries, user roles, inputs, outputs, integrations, and known costly failures. Generic prompts produce generic edge cases.

intro.html: AI can be a cheap source of additional suspicion. That is valuable in QA, provided suspicion eventually becomes a reproducible check.

sections.title: 1. Give it the contract
sections.html: Describe what should happen and what must never happen. Include meaningful constraints rather than only a feature name.

sections.title: 2. Ask from several failure angles
sections.html: Request boundary values, missing data, duplicated actions, stale state, wrong permissions, malformed inputs, timeouts, interruptions, and misuse that fits the system.

sections.title: 3. Triage the candidates
sections.html: Remove duplicates and impossible scenarios. Rank what remains by likelihood, impact, and cost to test.

sections.title: 4. Encode the useful ones
sections.html: Turn the surviving cases into automated tests, acceptance examples, monitoring rules, or a concise manual checklist. The artifact, not the brainstorm, is the payoff.

editorialCuration.reason: Publish as an AI-assisted QA ideation protocol with an explicit hypothesis-to-test boundary and no claim that model-generated cases are complete or correct.
